why: Brenton’s Appendix opens with eight notes too long for the margin column. Each prints as a footnote at the foot of the page, at the verse it discusses, with a numbered caller at the words it is about, as the front matter’s notes are set; the label naming the verse goes, since the note stands there. The passages the Appendix supplies from Codex Alexandrinus stand in their books (edition/alexandrinus.json), so nothing of it prints after Revelation.

EXO 28:29.label: Exodus 28.
paragraphs: And thou shalt make upon the oracle two golden rings
EXO 28:29.why: The Complutensian verses 23–28 fall between Brenton’s 22 and 29, where his caller stands in 1844 (vol. 1 p. 113: Alex. + See Appendix.); their numbers print as the note’s own.

2SA 5:18.label: 2 Kings (2 Sam.) 5. 18.—
2SA 5:18.why: Brenton’s margin note, Lit. Titans. Heb. Rephaim. See Appendix., stands before the word in the Bagster printings (1879 p. 423), and in 1844 (vol. 1 p. 358) without the pointer; the note takes the same place, and the margin note keeps its other words.

JOB 25:2.label: Job 25. 2.—
JOB 25:2.why: Brenton’s caller stands before beginning, his rendering of προοίμιον, in 1844 (vol. 2 p. 65), where his margin note also says See Appendix.

JOB 39:13.label: Job 39. 13.—
JOB 39:13.why: Brenton’s caller stands at the head of the verse in 1844 (vol. 2 p. 75), where his margin note also says See Appendix.

PSA 41:5.label: Psalm 41 (42):4.—
PSA 41:5.why: The note discusses the whole verse, so its caller stands at the start, consistently with the other whole-verse Appendix notes. Brenton’s margin note, See Appendix., stands at the end of the verse in the Bagster printings; his 1844 text (vol. 2 p. 97) leaves the verse unmarked. The fourth verse by the Hebrew’s count, which the Appendix’s label gives, is his fifth, since he counts the title.

PRO 8:5.label: Proverbs 8. 5.—
paragraphs: It is frequently the case in Proverbs
PRO 8:5.why: Brenton’s Appendix pointer, “For the uses of ἄκακος and πανοῦργος in this book, see Appendix.”, has its ζ caller immediately before simple in Proverbs 8:5 in the 1879 physical p. 810 and 1900 physical p. 806 scans (printed p. 794 in both), in “O ye ζsimple, understand subtlety”. The transferred Appendix note takes this printed caller’s place. The separate Appendix paragraph is not evidence from this pointer review.

ISA 2:6.label: Isaiah 2. 6.—
ISA 2:6.why: Brenton’s margin note, Or, aliens, see Appendix., stands before the word in every printing (1844 vol. 2 p. 188; 1879 p. 853; 1900 p. 849); the note takes the same place, and the margin note keeps its other words.

EZK 16:44.label: Jezekiel 16. 44.—
paragraphs: The most obvious meaning of παραβολὴ
EZK 16:44.why: Brenton’s caller stands before proverb, his rendering of παραβολή, in 1844 (vol. 2 p. 318), where his margin note also says See Appendix.
